title: The future is not always open

verification.evidence: Abstract: "We demonstrate the breakdown of several fundamentals of Lorentzian causality theory in low regularity. Most notably, chronological futures (defined naturally using locally Lipschitz curves) may be non-open, and may differ from the corresponding sets defined via piecewise C^1-curves. By refining the notion of a causal bubble ... we characterize spacetimes for which such phenomena can occur ... The phenomena described here are, in particular, relevant for recent synthetic approaches to low regularity Lorentzian geometry ..."

notes: Located and abstract-read in this session in response to the F1 pointer (lead-formulation evidence packet 2026-09-11T23:43). Peer-reviewed: Crossref confirms Lett. Math. Phys. 110(1), 83-103 (2020).

assessment.reason: F1 pointer on C^0 causal-structure degeneracy. This is a low-regularity causality-theory result, not a statement about asymptotically flat developments of the Einstein equations; it is therefore NOT attached to any of the four classes and must not be cited as evidence that the AF-SCC-C0 class is degenerate. title: The nature of spacetime singularities
venue: 100 Years of Relativity - Space-Time Structure: Einstein and Beyond (A. Ashtekar, ed.), World Scientific, pp. 76-92 (2005); arXiv:gr-qc/0503112 (survey)

verification.evidence: Abstract: "Present knowledge about the nature of spacetime singularities in the context of classical general relativity is surveyed. The status of the BKL picture of cosmological singularities and its relevance to the cosmic censorship hypothesis are discussed. It is shown how insights on cosmic censorship also arise in connection with the idea of weak null singularities inside black holes. ... Remarks are made on possible future directions in research on spacetime singularities."

notes: Located and abstract-read in this session in response to the F1 pointer. SURVEY article; Crossref confirms book chapter in '100 Years of Relativity', pp. 76-92, World Scientific (2005).

assessment.reason: F1 pointer on Kerr-data extendibility and genericity. Survey-level only: it proves no theorem and must NOT be cited as evidence that Kerr data admit a smooth extension, nor as class evidence for AF-SCC-C0. Usable only as background framing, if at all.
